## Results

- Top-1 accuracy 0.903 (95% CI 0.899-0.908) and top-3 0.978 on a 15,636-record held-out test split
- 98.3% of predictions land in the correct aircraft system; 63% of the remaining errors are same-subsystem near misses
- Predictions shown at 70% confidence or higher, which is 93% of answerable records, are correct 94.6% of the time (n = 14,795)
- Re-measuring what the app actually served caught a train/serve pooling mismatch that had cut production accuracy from 0.897 to 0.756 for three months
- Flat and hierarchical variants are statistically indistinguishable (sign test p = 0.33), so the simpler one ships

## The problem

Maintainers hand-assign one of roughly 1,300 Work Unit Codes to every KC-135 maintenance record. Miscoded records reduce the quality of reliability, sustainment and readiness analysis built on that data.

## What I built

I merged and deduplicated records from two extracts covering 2019 to 2026, then fed the discrepancy and corrective-action text to a ModernBERT-large classifier over 1,251 codes, trained with class-weighted cross-entropy and hierarchical system and subsystem auxiliary losses. I evaluated the served model on held-out records, reporting accuracy separately from label coverage, calibration by confidence band, and errors broken down by the WUC hierarchy.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## What it is for

Supports the WUC coding decision on completed maintenance records. The top-3 suggestions plus a confidence band send low-confidence records to QC review. The confusion pairs found (for example, codes used interchangeably across bases) are direct feedback to data owners on inconsistent coding that distorts downstream analysis.
:::

## Tools

Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, ModernBERT-large, scikit-learn, pandas, Streamlit, Altair, Ollama (Gemma 4, local)

[Accuracy is scored against QC-corrected labels. Training data and model weights are CUI and are not public.]{.fine}
